69248-atlanta-offering-poems.description: A book by Frances E. W. Harper. how fleeting are his years  With their smiles and their tears;  Can it be that God does care  For such atoms as we are? Then outspake this grain of sand  “I was fashioned by His hand  In the star lit realms of space  I was made to have a place.

arxiv-2012-07782.title: A Quantum Invariant of Links in T 2 × I T^{2}\times I with Volume Conjecture Behavior
arxiv-2012-07782.creator: Joe Boninger
arxiv-2012-07782.description: Abstract . We define a polynomial invariant J n T J_{n}^{T} of links in the thickened torus. We call J n T J^{T}_{n} the n n th toroidal colored Jones polynomial, and show it satisfies many properties of the original colored Jones polynomial. Most significantly, J n T J_{n}^{T} exhibits volume conjecture behavior.

arxiv-2112-07387.title: Decomposition of higher-order Wright convex functions revisited
arxiv-2112-07387.creator: Zsolt Páles, Mahmood Kamil Shihab
arxiv-2112-07387.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zsolt Páles, Mahmood Kamil Shihab. In 2009, Maksa and Páles established an extension of the decomposition theorem of Ng in the context of higher-order convexity notions. They proved that a real function is Wright convex of order n n if and only if it can be decomposed as the sum of a convex function of order n n and a polynomial function of order at most n n . Their proof was based on transfinite tools in the background.

arxiv-2312-10792.title: Probing the galactic and extragalactic gravitational wave backgrounds with space-based interferometers
arxiv-2312-10792.creator: and M. Peloso
arxiv-2312-10792.description: Abstract We employ the formalism developed in [ 1 ] and [ 2 ] to study the prospect of detecting an anisotropic Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background (SGWB) with the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) alone, and combined with the proposed space-based interferometer Taiji. Previous analyses have been performed in the frequency domain only.

arxiv-2405-17109.title: Left-Linear Completion with AC Axioms Thanks: The research described in this article is partly supported by JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number JP22K11900.
arxiv-2405-17109.creator: Johannes Niederhauser ORCID:0000-0002-8662-6834, Nao Hirokawa ORCID:0000-0002-8499-0501, Aart Middeldorp ORCID:0000-0001-7366-8464
arxiv-2405-17109.description: Abstract . We revisit completion modulo equational theories for left-linear term rewrite systems where unification modulo the theory is avoided and the normal rewrite relation can be used in order to decide validity questions. To that end, we give a new correctness proof for finite runs and establish a simulation result between the two inference systems known from the literature.

arxiv-2406-07169.title: RDM: Recurrent Diffusion Model for Human Motion Generation
arxiv-2406-07169.description: Abstract Human motion generation is a challenging task due to its high dimensionality and the difficulty of generating fine-grained motions. Diffusion methods have been proposed due to their high sample quality and expressiveness. Early approaches treat the entire sequence as a whole, which is computationally expensive and restricts sequence length. In contrast, autoregressive diffusion models generate longer sequences.

arxiv-2506-19725.title: Exploring Low-Dimensional Magnetism in Cobalt Vanadates, A {A} CoV 2 O 7 ( A {A} = Ca, Sr) : Crystal Growth and Magnetic Properties of Effective Spin-1/2 Zigzag Chains
arxiv-2506-19725.creator: Anzar Ali, Guratinder Kaur, Arvind Maurya, Isha, Kathrin Küster, Ulrich Starke, Pascal Puphal, Arvind Kumar Yogi, Masahiko Isobe
arxiv-2506-19725.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anzar Ali, Guratinder Kaur, Arvind Maurya, Isha, Kathrin Küster, Ulrich Starke, Pascal Puphal, Arvind Kumar Yogi, Masahiko Isobe. We report the successful growth of high-quality single crystals of A {A} CoV 2 O 7 ( A {A} = Ca, Sr), a quasi-one-dimensional zigzag chain compound containing Co 2+ ions, using the optical floating zone method. The crystal growth was stabilized under high-pressure argon-oxygen gas with slow growth rates, overcoming challenges associated with the incongruent melting behavior of this material.

arxiv-2509-08049.title: Similarities in the evaporation of saturated solitons and black holes
arxiv-2509-08049.creator: Giacomo Contri ID, Gia Dvali, Otari Sakhelashvili
arxiv-2509-08049.description: Abstract It has been suggested some time ago that many black hole properties are not specific to gravity, but rather are shared by a large class of objects, the so-called saturons, that saturate the quantum field theoretic upper bound on microstate degeneracy. By now, various aspects of this universality have been understood and demonstrated in a number of explicit examples.

arxiv-2511-15310.title: Refractive indices of photochemical haze analogs for Solar System and exoplanet applications : a cross-laboratory comparative study between the PAMPRE and COSmIC experimental set-ups
arxiv-2511-15310.creator: T. Drant, E. Sciamma-O’Brien, L. Jovanovic, Z. Perrin, L. Maratrat, L. Vettier, E. Garcia-Caurel, J.-B. Brubach, D.H. Wooden, T.L. Roush, C.L. Ricketts, P. Rannou
arxiv-2511-15310.description: Abstract Previous observations of Titan, Pluto and Solar System gas giants along with recent observations of exoplanet atmospheres with the James Webb Space Telescope taught us that photochemical hazes are ubiquitous and form in a variety of temperature, gas composition and irradiation environments.

arxiv-2512-09617.title: FROMAT: Multiview Material Appearance Transfer via Few-Shot Self-Attention Adaptation
arxiv-2512-09617.creator: Hubert Kompanowski, Varun Jampani, Aaryaman Vasishta, Binh-Son Hua
arxiv-2512-09617.description: Abstract Multiview diffusion models have rapidly emerged as a powerful tool for content creation with spatial consistency across viewpoints, offering rich visual realism without requiring explicit geometry and appearance representation. However, compared to meshes or radiance fields, existing multiview diffusion models offer limited appearance manipulation, particularly in terms of material, texture, or style.

arxiv-2602-22328.title: Resonant Zener Interferometry in van der Waals Heterostructures
arxiv-2602-22328.creator: Nisarga Paul, Gil Refael
arxiv-2602-22328.description: Abstract We demonstrate the presence of quantum interference effects in van der Waals heterostructures subject to in-plane electric fields. The in-plane field F F accelerates carriers through a hybridized band edge, and interlayer Zener tunneling occurs by distinct pathways, resulting in a solid-state quantum interferometer with imprints in transport observables.

pmc-10610428.title: Road Impact on Plant Colonization in the Arid Timanfaya National Park
pmc-10610428.creator: María Bernardos, Natalia Sierra Cornejo, Antonio Daniel Torres Hassan, Raimundo Cabrera, José Ramón Arévalo
pmc-10610428.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Roads have the potential to alter local environmental conditions, such as the availability of water and nutrients, and rapidly create suitable habitats for the establishment of both native and non-native plant species, transforming the ecosystems. This is a challenge in Timanfaya National Park and Los Volcanes Natural Park on Lanzarote Island, protected areas that have experienced primary succession after recent volcanic eruptions. In arid ecosystems, changes in abiotic conditions along roadsides might facilitate colonization and plant growth.

pmc-10656660.title: Factors Associated With Work Engagement of Nurses During the Fifth Wave of the COVID-19 Pandemic in Japan: Web-Based Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-10656660.creator: Kei Muroi, Mami Ishitsuka, Tomoko Hachisuka, Itsuka Shibata, Tomohiko Ikeda, Daisuke Hori, Shotaro Doki, Tsukasa Takahashi, Shin-ichiro Sasahara, Ichiyo Matsuzaki
pmc-10656660.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic has brought to light the prevalence of mental health issues among nurses. Work engagement (WE) is a concept that describes work-related positive psychological states and is of importance within mental health measures. There is, however, a lack of research on factors associated with the WE of nurses during the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-11396099.title: Effect of Kinematic Chain Exercise Protocol on Throwing Performance and Shoulder Muscle Strength among University Shot Put Athletes—A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-11396099.creator: Vinod Kumar Kanakapura Chananke Gowda, Shenbaga Sundaram Subramanian, Riziq Allah Mustafa Gaowgzeh, Samira Ahmed Alsenany, Sally Mohammed Farghaly Abdelaliem, Amany Anwar Saeed Alabdullah, Alkhateeb M Afnan, Darren Warburton, Filippo Migliorini
pmc-11396099.description: Background/Objectives: This study looks at how a kinematic chain exercise regimen that targets the lower, core, and upper body affects university shot put participants’ shoulder muscle strength and throwing efficiency. This study fills an apparent research void on shot put training approaches by presenting a comprehensive kinematic chain workout program.

pmc-13616692.title: Experimental assessment of computationally nominated small molecules targeting the YAP–TEAD interface in Hippo pathway-altered mesothelioma cell models
pmc-13616692.creator: Glen J. Weiss, Joseph C. Loftus, David W. Mallery, Nhan L. Tran
pmc-13616692.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aberrant activation of the Hippo–YAP/TAZ–TEAD transcriptional axis is a recurrent feature of multiple solid tumors and contributes to tumor maintenance, lineage plasticity, and therapeutic resistance. Recent medicinal chemistry has shown that TEAD proteins are druggable, but the rate at which in silico screening nominates compounds that prove functionally active in cells remains poorly defined, and negative validation results are rarely reported.
